translations.text: In the eighth month of the second year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
The Lord was very angry with your fathers.
You shall say to them, “This is what the Lord Almighty says: Return to me, says the Lord of hosts, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts.”

Do not be like your fathers, whom the earlier prophets rebuked, saying, “This is what the Lord Almighty says: Turn away from all your evil ways and your evil deeds.” But they did not hear or pay attention to me, says the Lord.
Where are your fathers? And did the prophets live forever?

But receive my words and my laws, which I command by my Spirit to my servants the prophets, who came to your fathers. They answered and said, “Just as the Lord Almighty determined to deal with us according to our ways and our deeds, so he has dealt with us.”
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is Arats, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
I saw in a vision at night, and there was a man riding a bay horse. He stood between two densely wooded mountains, and behind him were bay, dappled, and white horses.
I said, “What are these, my lord?” The angel who was speaking with me said, “I will show you what these are.”
The man standing between the mountains answered and said to me, “These are the ones whom the Lord sent to travel throughout the earth.”
They answered the angel of the Lord who stood between the mountains and said, “We have traveled throughout the whole earth, and the whole earth is inhabited and at rest.”
The angel answered and said, “Lord Almighty, how long will you withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you have disregarded into this seventieth year?”
The Lord Almighty answered the angel who was speaking with me with kind words and words of comfort.
The angel who was speaking with me said, “Proclaim this: This is what the Lord Almighty says: I have been intensely jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.
And I am very angry with the nations that joined together to attack them, because I was only a little angry with them, but those nations joined together to attack them and bring harm.”
Therefore the Lord says this: I will return to Jerusalem with compassion, and my house will be rebuilt, says the Lord Almighty, and a measuring line will again be stretched over Jerusalem.

And the angel who spoke with me said to me: Cry out and say: The Lord Almighty says this: The cities will again overflow with good things, and the Lord will have mercy on Zion and will again take pleasure in Jerusalem.
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were four horns.
I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel.”
The Lord showed me four carpenters.

I said, “What have these come to do?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel and crushed them, so that none of them raised his head. These have come out to sharpen them in their hands—the four horns, the nations that raised a horn against the Lord’s land to scatter it.”
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a man holding a measuring line in his hand.
I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem and see how wide and how long it is.”
The angel who was speaking with me had taken his place and was standing there, and another angel was coming out to meet him.
He said to him, “Run and speak to that young man, and say: Jerusalem will be built up fruitfully because of the multitude of people and livestock within it.
And I will be a wall of fire all around it, and I will dwell in glory within it.”
Ho! Ho! Flee from the land of the north, says the Lord, for I will gather you from the four winds of heaven, says the Lord.
Make your way to Zion and escape, you who inhabit the daughter of Babylon.
For the Lord Almighty says this: After glory he sent me to the nations that plundered you, for whoever comes near you is like someone who strikes the pupil of his own eye.
For look, I will bring my hand against them, and those who enslaved them will become plunder. Then you will know that the Lord Almighty sent me.
Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, for behold, I will come and dwell among you, says the Lord.
Many nations will take refuge in the Lord on that day and become his people, and they will dwell among you. Then you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
The Lord will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and he will once again take pleasure in Jerusalem.
All flesh will fear before the Lord, for he has risen from his holy clouds.
And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and Satan stood at his right hand to oppose him.
The Lord said to Satan, “May the Lord rebuke you, Satan! May the Lord who chose Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not like a firebrand rescued from the fire?”
Joshua was dressed in filthy clothes and stood before the angel of the Lord.

He answered and said to those standing before him, “Remove the filthy clothes from him.” And he said to him, “Behold, I have taken your lawlessness away from you. Dress him in a robe reaching to his feet.”
“And put a holy turban on his head.” They put a holy turban on his head and dressed him in clothes, while the angel of the Lord stood there.
The angel of the Lord solemnly charged Joshua, saying:
The Lord Almighty says this: If you walk in my ways and keep my commands, you will judge my house; and if you guard my courts, I will give you people who walk among those who stand there.
“But listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men who read omens. Behold, I am bringing my servant, the Branch.
For on the stone that I have placed before Joshua there are seven eyes. Behold, I will carve a hollow, says the Lord Almighty, and I will probe all the lawlessness of that land in one day.
On that day, says the Lord Almighty, each of you will invite his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.”
The angel who spoke to me returned and awakened me, as a man is awakened from his sleep.
He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “Behold, I see a lampstand of cast gold, with a bowl on top of it, and seven lamps on it, and seven spouts for the lamps that are on it.
And there are two olive trees above it, one to the right of the lighted bowl and one to the left.”
I asked the angel who spoke to me, “What are these, my lord?”
The angel who spoke to me answered and said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
The angel answered and said to me, “This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by a great army and not by strength, but by my Spirit,’ says the Lord Almighty.
Who are you, great mountain standing before Zerubbabel? And I will bring out the stone of inheritance, the equality of graces to be bestowed on him.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Zerubbabel’s hands laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will raise it up. Then you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
For who has despised the small days? He will rejoice, and they will see the tin stone in Zerubbabel’s hand. These are the seven eyes that look over all the earth.”
I answered and said to him, “And what are the two olive trees standing to the right and left of the lampstand?”
I asked him again, “What are the two olive branches held by the two golden lamp spouts that pour out and lift up the golden [?]?”
He said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.” He said to me, “These are the sons of abundance who stand before the Lord of all the earth.”
I turned, lifted my eyes, and looked, and behold, there was a flying sickle.
He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.”

He said to me, “These are the curses that go out over the face of the whole earth, for through them every thief will be punished with death, and through them everyone who swears falsely will be punished with death.”

“I will send it out,” says the Lord Almighty, “and it will enter the houses of thieves and the houses of those who swear falsely by my name. It will remain inside each one's house and destroy it, along with its timber and its stones.”
The angel who was speaking with me came out and said to me, “Look with your own eyes and see what is coming out.” I said, “What is it?”
He said to me, “This is the measuring basket that is coming out.” He said, “This is their wickedness throughout the whole earth.”
And there was a lead weight being lifted up, and a woman was sitting inside the measuring basket.
He said, “This is wickedness.” He threw her into the measuring basket and threw the lead weight over its opening.
I raised my eyes and saw two women coming out, with wind in their wings. Their wings were like the wings of a hoopoe, and they lifted the measuring basket between earth and heaven.
I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “Where are they taking the measuring basket?”
He said to me, “To build a house for it in the land of the Babylonians and prepare it. They will set it there on its prepared foundation.”
Again I raised my eyes and looked, and there were four chariots coming out from between two mountains. The mountains were mountains of bronze.
The first chariot had chestnut horses, and the second chariot had black horses.
And in the third chariot were white horses, and in the fourth chariot were horses of various colors, dappled.
I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
The angel who spoke with me answered and said: These are the four winds of heaven, which go out to stand before the Lord of all the earth.
The chariot with the black horses went out toward the northern land, and the white horses went out after them. The chestnut horses went out toward the southern land.
The speckled horses went out, seeking to travel throughout the whole earth. He said, “Go and travel throughout the earth.” And they traveled throughout the earth.
He cried out and said to me, “Look, those going out toward the northern land have quieted my anger in the northern land.”
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
“Take for me from among the exiles, from their rulers, their capable men, and their learned men. On that day, enter the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who has come from Babylon.
Take gold and silver, make crowns, and place them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
Say to him, ‘This is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, a man whose name is Rising! He will spring up from beneath himself and build the Lord's house.
He will take strength, sit and rule on his throne, and there will be a priest at his right hand. There will be a counsel of peace between the two of them.’
The crown will be for those who wait, for his capable men, and for those who know him, as a favor to the son of Zephaniah, and for the songs of the Lord's house.”

And those among them who are far away will come and build the house of the Lord, and you will know that the Lord Almighty sent me to you. And this will happen if you truly listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev,
And he sent from Bethel Sharezer and Abusad, kings, and their men to entreat the Lord.
and to say to the priests who were in the house of the Lord Almighty and to the prophets, “Did holiness enter there in the fifth month?” For they had done this for many years.
The word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying:
Speak to all the people of this land and to the priests, and say: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth or seventh months for these seventy years, did you really fast for me?
“And when you eat and drink, is it not you yourselves who eat and drink?”
Are these not the words that the Lord spoke through his earlier prophets, while Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, with its surrounding towns, and the hill country and the plain were inhabited?
And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying:
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Judge with justice, and show mercy and compassion, each to his brother.
Do not oppress the widow, the orphan, the foreigner, or the poor, and let no one harbor resentment against his neighbor in his heart.
But they refused to listen. Instead, they foolishly turned their backs and made their ears heavy so that they would not hear.

They made their hearts disobedient so that they would not hear my laws or the words that the Lord Almighty sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. And great anger came from the Lord Almighty.
And it will happen that, just as they spoke and did not listen to him, so they will cry out and he will not listen to them, says the Lord Almighty.
I will cast them out among all the nations they do not know, and the land will be devastated after them, so that no one will go out or return. They made the choice land a wasteland.
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty:
I have been intensely jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion, and with great anger I have been jealous for her.
Thus says the Lord: I will return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty, the Holy Mountain.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women will again sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of their great age.
And the squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in its squares.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: If something seems too difficult to the remnant of that people in those days, will it also be too difficult for me? says the Lord Almighty.
The Lord Almighty says this: Behold, I will save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.
I will bring them and settle them in the midst of Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God in truth and righteousness.

Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words in these days from the mouths of the prophets, from the day you laid the foundation of the house of the Lord Almighty and since this temple was built.

For before those days, wages for people were of no benefit, and wages for animals were of no value. There was no peace for anyone going out or coming in because of affliction, and I will send everyone against his neighbor.
But now I will not treat the remnant of that people as I did in the former days, says the Lord Almighty.
Instead, I will show peace. The vineyard will give its fruit, the land will give its crops, and the heavens will give their dew. I will cause the remnant of my people to inherit all these things.
And just as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Take courage, and let your hands be strong.
For thus says the Lord Almighty: Just as I planned to afflict you when your fathers provoked me to anger, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not relent,
so in these days I have resolved and planned to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Take courage.
These are the things you must do: Speak the truth, each to his neighbor, and render just judgments that bring peace at your gates.
Let none of you plan evil against his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love false oaths, for I hate all these things, says the Lord Almighty.
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying:

Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fourth fast and the fifth fast, the seventh fast and the tenth fast will become occasions of gladness and joy and festivals of good things for the house of Judah. Be joyful, and love truth and peace.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Many peoples and the inhabitants of many cities will come again.
The inhabitants of one city will gather in another city and say, “Let us go to plead before the Lord and seek the presence of God Almighty. I too will go.”
Many peoples will come to seek the presence of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem and to seek the Lord’s favor.

Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of the hem of a Jewish man’s garment and say, “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.”
An oracle of the word of the Lord against the land of Hadrach, and his sacrifice is in Damascus, for the Lord sees humanity and all the tribes of Israel.
And in Hamath, within its borders, Tyre and Sidon, because they showed great contempt.
Tyre built her fortifications and piled up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
Therefore the Lord will take possession of her and [?] her strength in the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see and be afraid, and Gaza will suffer greatly, as will Ekron, because she was put to shame over her transgressions. The king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
Foreigners will dwell in Ashdod, and I will break down the pride of the foreigners.

I will remove their blood from their mouths and their abominations from between their teeth. They too will remain for our God and will become like commanders of thousands in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusite.
I will appoint a protector for my house so that no one may pass through or return, and no one who persecutes them will come against them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.
Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your King is coming to you, righteous and a savior, humble and riding on a donkey, on a young foal.

He will destroy the chariots from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem, and the bow of war will be shattered. There will be abundance and peace from the nations, and he will rule over the waters from sea to sea and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.
And you, by the blood of your covenant, have released your prisoners from a waterless pit.
Dwell in strongholds, prisoners of your people, and in place of one day of your exile I will repay you double.
For I will bend you, Judah, for myself like a bow, and I will fill it with Ephraim. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against the sons of the Greeks, and I will wield you like a warrior's steel sword.
The Lord will watch over them, and his arrow will go forth like lightning. The Lord, the Lord Almighty, will sound the trumpet and advance with the shaking of his threats.
The Lord Almighty will protect them, and they will consume them and bury them with slingstones. They will drink their blood like wine and fill the bowls like the altar.
The Lord their God will save them on that day, his people like sheep, for holy stones roll over his land.
For whatever is good is his, and whatever is beautiful belongs to him: grain for young men and wine that makes maidens glad.
Ask the Lord for rain in its seasons, the early and the late rain. The Lord has made wondrous things, and he will give them winter rain, grass to each one in the field.

For the diviners spoke of troubles, and the fortune-tellers spoke of false visions and false dreams and offered comfort in vain. Therefore they withered like sheep and suffered, because there was no healing.
My anger burned against the shepherds, and I will punish the lambs. The Lord God Almighty will visit his flock, the house of Judah, and prepare them for himself like a beautiful warhorse.
From him he kept watch, and from him he made preparations, and from him was his bow held high; and from him everyone who drives out will go forth together.
They will be like warriors who trample the mud in the roads during battle. They will fight because the Lord is with them, and those riding horses will be put to shame.

I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will settle them because I have loved them, and they will be as though I had not turned away from them, for I am the Lord their God, and I will hear them.
They will be like the warriors of Ephraim, and their hearts will rejoice as though from wine. Their children will see and be glad, and their hearts will rejoice in the Lord.
I will signal to them and gather them, because I have saved them. They will become as numerous as they were before.
I will sow them among the nations, and those who are far away will remember me. They will raise their children and return.
I will bring them back from the land of the Egyptians and gather them from the Assyrians. I will bring them into Gilead and Lebanon, and not one of them will be missing.

They will pass through the narrow sea and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the rivers will dry up. All the pride of the Assyrians will be removed, and the dominion of the Egyptians will be destroyed.
I will strengthen them in the Lord their God, and they will boast in his name, says the Lord.
Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire consume your cedars.
Let the cypresses lament, because the cedars have fallen, because the mighty have been greatly afflicted. Lament, oaks of Bashan, because the densely planted forest has been destroyed.
The sound of shepherds lamenting, for their greatness has been laid waste; the sound of lions roaring, for the heights of the Jordan have been laid waste.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Tend the flock destined for slaughter.
Their owners slaughtered and sold them, saying, “Blessed be the Lord! We have grown rich!” And their shepherds felt no sorrow for them.

Therefore I will no longer spare the inhabitants of this land, says the Lord. And behold, I will hand over each person into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king. They will strike them, and I will not rescue them from their hands.
I will shepherd the flock destined for slaughter in the land of the Canaanites. I will take two staffs for myself: I will call one Beauty, and I will call the second Lot. And I will tend the flock.
I will remove the three shepherds in one month, and my soul will grow weary of them, because their souls also cried out against me.
I say, “I will not shepherd you. Let the one destined to die die, and let the one destined to perish perish. Let those who remain each eat the flesh of their neighbor.”
I took my staff, Beauty, and cast it away to dissolve my covenant, which I had made with all the peoples.
It will be dissolved on that day, and the Canaanites will know concerning the flock in my care that this is the word of the Lord.
I said to them, “If it seems good in your eyes, give me my wages; but if not, say so.” And they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.

And the Lord said to me: Cast that into the furnace, and examine whether it is genuine, as I was found genuine on their behalf. And I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them into the furnace in the house of the Lord.
I cast away the second staff, Lot, to dissolve my covenant between Judah and Israel.
The Lord says to me, “Take for yourself again the equipment of a foolish shepherd.”

For behold, I will raise up a foolish shepherd over the land. He will not care for the weak, seek the scattered, heal the injured, or nourish the healthy. He will eat the flesh of the choicest animals and crush their feet.
O worthless shepherds, who strike down the flock! A sword against his arm and against his right eye! His arm will wither completely, and his right eye will become utterly blind.
The oracle of the word of the Lord concerning Israel. The Lord speaks, who stretched out the heavens, laid the foundations of the earth, and establishes the human spirit within a person.
Look, I will make Jerusalem like shaking thresholds for all the peoples around it, and Jerusalem will be besieged in Judah.
And on that day I will make Jerusalem like a stone to be trampled by all the nations. Everyone who tramples on it will mock it with derision, and all the nations of the earth will gather against it.

On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. I will open my eyes over the house of Judah, and I will strike all the horses of the nations with blindness.
And the commanders of Judah will say in their hearts, “We will find the inhabitants of Jerusalem through the Lord Almighty, their God.”

On that day I will make the commanders of Judah like burning brands among wood and like flaming torches among reeds. They will devour all the surrounding peoples to the right and to the left, and Jerusalem will again dwell by itself in Jerusalem.

And the Lord will save the tents of Judah as in the beginning, so that the boasting of the house of David and the pride of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not exalt themselves over the house of Judah.

On that day the Lord will protect all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. The weak among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David will be like the house of God, like the angel of the Lord before them.
On that day I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

I will pour out a spirit of grace and compassion upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem. They will look to me whom they pierced, and they will mourn over him as over a beloved one, and lament bitterly as over a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning for pomegranate trees cut down in the plain.
The land will mourn, each family separately: the family of the house of David separately, and their wives separately; the family of the house of Nathan separately, and their wives separately;
the family of the house of Levi separately, and their wives separately; the family of the house of Simeon separately, and their wives separately;
all the remaining families separately, and their wives separately.
On that day every place will be opened to the house of David for change and for sprinkling.
On that day the Lord will remove the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the false prophets and the unclean spirits from the land.

If anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who gave birth to him will say to him, “You shall not live, because you have spoken lies in the name of the Lord.” And his father and mother who gave birth to him will stop him from prophesying.
On that day the prophets will each be ashamed of their visions when they prophesy, and they will put on hairy mantles because they lied.
And he will say, “I am not a prophet, but a farmer, and a man begot me from my youth.”
And I will say to him, “What are those wounds between your hands?” And he will say, “Those are the wounds I received in the house of my beloved.”

“Awake, sword, against my shepherd and against the man who is his companion,” says the Lord Almighty. “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the shepherds.”
“On that day,” says the Lord, “two parts in it will perish and disappear, and the third will remain in it.

I will bring the third part through fire and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. He will call upon my name, and I will hear him. I will say, ‘This is my people,’ and he will say, ‘You are the Lord my God.’”
Look, the days of the Lord will come, and your plunder will be divided among you.

And he will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle, and the city will be captured, the houses plundered, and the women violated. Half the city will go into captivity, but the remnant of my people will not be destroyed from the city.
The Lord will go out and wage war against those nations, as on the day of his battle, on the day of war.

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, opposite Jerusalem to the east. The Mount of Olives will split, half toward the east and half toward the sea, forming a very great chasm. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half toward the south.

And the valley of my mountains will be blocked, and the valley of the mountains will extend as far as Asael. It will be blocked as it was blocked by the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And the Lord my God will come and arrive, and all the holy ones with him.
And on that day there will be no light, and it will be cold and clear for one day.
And that day will be known to the Lord; it will be neither day nor night, and at evening there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out of Jerusalem, half of it into the eastern sea and half into the western sea. It will be the same in summer and spring.
And the Lord will be king over all the earth. On that day the Lord will be one, and his name one.

Encircling all the land, the wilderness from Geba to Rimmon on the southern side of Jerusalem; and Ramah will stand in its place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the site of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and to the Tower of Hananel, to the king’s winepresses.
And people will live in it, and there will no longer be any curses, and Jerusalem will dwell securely.

And these will be the plagues with which the Lord will strike all the nations that gathered their armies against Jerusalem: their flesh will melt away while they are standing on their feet, their eyes will melt out of their sockets, and their tongues will melt away in their mouths.
And on that day great terror from the Lord will fall upon them. Each will seize his neighbor’s hand and lock his own hand with his neighbor’s hand.
And Judah will fight at Jerusalem and gather the wealth of all the surrounding nations: gold, silver, and very large quantities of clothing.
And the plagues upon the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the livestock in those camps will be like this same plague.
And all who remain from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the Lord God Almighty, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
And whichever of all the nations of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord God Almighty, will have no rain upon it.

And if the nation of the Egyptians does not go up and come, then upon them will fall the plagues with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
The same will happen because of the sins of the Egyptians and the sins of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
On that day, “Holiness to the Lord” will be on the horses’ bridles. And the pots in the house of the Lord will be like the bowls before the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be consecrated to the Lord Almighty. All who offer sacrifices will come and take some of them and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty.
